This implies that Atomoxetine may influence Htr2c through its pharmacological properties, even if it does not directly bind to Htr2c. The connection is further supported by the observed participation of Htr6, which is part of the serotonin receptor family and is linked to Htr2c. Thus, the relationship between Atomoxetine and Htr2c is mediated through a chain of molecular interactions involving serotonin receptors and the broader antidepressant class. The evidence highlights a potential mechanism by which Atomoxetine may modulate Htr2c activity, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
